BASTION decomposition

fit_BASTION.Rd

Bayesian trend and seasonal decomposition with locally adaptive priors.

Usage

fit_BASTION(y, Ks, X = NULL, Outlier = FALSE, cl = 0.95,
  sparse = FALSE, obsSV = "const", nchains = 2, nsave = 1000,
  nburn = 1000, nskip = 4, verbose = TRUE, save_samples = FALSE,
  D_trend = 2L)

Arguments

y

Numeric observation vector or univariate time series.

Ks

List of fixed seasonal periods.

X

Optional regression design matrix.

Outlier

Include outliers with a horseshoe+ prior at all observations (default FALSE).

cl

Pointwise credible interval probability.

sparse

Additional trend shrinkage option.

obsSV

Observation variance model: "const" or "SV".

nchains

Number of chains.

nsave

Saved draws per chain.

nburn

Burn-in sweeps per chain.

nskip

Discarded sweeps between saves; save every nskip+1 sweeps.

verbose

Display progress.

save_samples

Include posterior draws under draws.

D_trend

Trend difference order, 1 or 2 (default 2).

Value

An object of class bastion_fit. Let T be the number of observations, M the number of decomposition columns (including residual), D the total saved draws, K a seasonal period, and p the number of regression coefficients.

time

Observation times, length T. Uses time(y) for a time series and observation numbers otherwise.

observed

Supplied observations, length T.

components

T by M data frame of posterior means. Columns are trend, seasonal_<period>, regression/outlier when fitted, and residual.

intervals

lower and upper, T by M data frames with matching component names and order.

seasonality

One named entry per seasonal component. Each contains recurring, a K by 3 data frame with mean, lower, upper; and deviation, a T by 3 data frame with mean, lower, upper.

regression

When fitted, coefficients is a p by 4 data frame with term, mean, lower, upper. Unnamed covariates use beta_1, beta_2, etc.

noise

sd has T rows for SV or one row for constant SD, with mean, lower, upper. Under SV, parameters has three rows with parameter, mean, lower, upper.

metadata

Fitting metadata includes cl, the credible-interval probability, and alpha = 1 - cl. Input seasonal periods, fitting arguments, and recurring positions under mapping$recurring_positions.

draws

Present only when save_samples=TRUE. index is a D by 3 data frame (draw, chain, iteration); components is D by T by M, including residuals. Each seasonality entry contains D by K recurring and D by T deviation matrices. Optional regression$coefficients is D by p. noise$sd is D by T under SV or D by 1 otherwise; SV noise$parameters is D by 3 (mu, phi, innovation_sd).

Details

BASTION decomposes a time series into a locally adaptive trend, one or more seasonal components, and optional regression and outlier components. The components are estimated jointly using Bayesian inference.

Supply seasonal periods in numbers of observations through Ks. For example, use list(12) for yearly seasonality in monthly data, or list(7, 365) for weekly and yearly seasonality in daily data. Each seasonal component combines a common recurring pattern with deviations that allow the pattern to evolve across cycles.

The trend uses second differences by default (D_trend = 2). Use D_trend = 1 for first differences. Setting sparse = TRUE applies stronger shrinkage to trend differences while retaining local adaptivity.

Use obsSV = "const" for constant observation variance or obsSV = "SV" to estimate observation variability over time. Set Outlier = TRUE to estimate a separate outlier component, and supply X to include regression effects.

Component estimates and observation standard deviations are returned in the units of the supplied data. Posterior means and credible intervals at the level specified by cl are returned whether or not posterior draws are retained. Set save_samples = TRUE to retain the draws.

Use print() for an overview of the fit, summary() for the component estimates, plot() for the decomposition, and plot_component() to inspect an individual component with credible intervals.

See also

simulate_BASTION

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Daily observations with fixed weekly and yearly periods
sim <- simulate_BASTION("daily", seed = 20)
fit_daily <- fit_BASTION(
  y = sim$y,
  Ks = list(7, 365),
  obsSV = "const", nchains = 1
)
plot(fit_daily)
plot_component(fit_daily, "seasonal_365", part = "recurring")

# A pattern repeating every 14 observations
sim <- simulate_BASTION("biweekly", seed = 21)
fit_biweekly <- fit_BASTION(
  y = sim$y,
  Ks = list(14),
  obsSV = "const", nchains = 1
)
plot_component(fit_biweekly, "seasonal_14")

# Hourly observations with daily and weekly periods
sim <- simulate_BASTION("hourly", seed = 22)
fit_hourly <- fit_BASTION(
  y = sim$y,
  Ks = list(24, 168),
  obsSV = "const", nchains = 1
)
plot(fit_hourly)
} # }
